summary.oneLiner: Record quarter on every line (vol 1.4m +29%, rev Rs.17,244 cr +37%, EBITDA Rs.3,596 cr +45%, PAT ~Rs.3,000 cr +42%) delivered *through* a hyperinflationary commodity shock (~4.5% of revenue), a ransomware shutdown and West-Asia supply disruptions that cost ~10% of volume. Margin still expanded to 20.9% (+110 bps YoY) on currency (USD-INR 94.4), mix and cost discipline. Exports (40% of rev) and EV (now 30% of domestic rev, double-digit EBITDA, Chetak turned EBITDA-positive) are the twin growth engines; capacity is now the binding constraint → 7m→9m units expansion underway.
summary.business: Bajaj Auto manufactures and sells motorcycles (commuter to premium sports bikes), electric scooters, and ICE/CNG/electric three-wheelers (passenger and goods carriers) plus the Qute quadricycle, along with related parts and accessories. It serves customers pan-India and in over 100 countries, spanning domestic retail, commercial/fleet buyers and export markets, with premium global motorcycle portfolios under KTM and Triumph.

currentContext.strengths: World's largest three-wheeler manufacturer and India's largest exporter of two- and three-wheelers, with presence in over 100 countries and over 32 million vehicles sold historically.|Domestic ICE three-wheeler market leadership with 73.8% overall share (79.1% passenger carriers, 52.5% goods carriers) and 87.9% share in CNG three-wheelers.|Export distribution strength: No.1 position in 9 of 15 key motorcycle export markets and leadership in 11 of 12 key commercial-vehicle export markets.|Premium brand portfolio (Pulsar, KTM, Triumph) sustained by continuous product refresh cadence and R&D investment -- reorganised R&D with expanded design/analysis/validation teams and a growing IP portfolio (patent filings across Powertrain, Vehicle and Integration domains).|Early-mover position in electric mobility: India's largest combined electric 2W+3W player, with Chetak among the top-two electric scooter brands (20.7% share) and pole position in the E3W (L5) segment achieved within three years of entry.
currentContext.strategies: Deepen competitiveness in the strategically important 125cc+ motorcycle segment through pricing and product interventions, including the Pulsar portfolio revamp and expansion.|Sustain and build market leadership in electric three-wheelers under the WEGO brand, with the longer-term intent of mirroring the scale of leadership achieved in the ICE three-wheeler category.|Scale up Chetak through recent product launches (e.g. Chetak C25) to grow market share in the electric two-wheeler segment.|Sustain export momentum, supported by improving macro-economic conditions across key international markets.|Nurture and expand the premium global portfolios under KTM and Triumph to further strengthen international market positioning.|Support KTM AG's turnaround for the coming year through portfolio prioritisation, product development, go-to-market execution, supply chain optimisation and organisational simplification, aiming to restore KTM to its original performance levels.|Build capability and leverage scale in Bajaj Auto Credit (BACL) to deliver an industry-class-leading financing performance.|Balance growth and profitability through robust operational management, mindful of margin pressure from rising commodity costs.|Operate a robust Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework to proactively scan, anticipate and convert emerging risks (geopolitical, regulatory, commodity, supply-chain, currency, technological) into strategic advantage.|The Company follows a formal Dividend Distribution Policy (regulation 43A of SEBI LODR) governing the parameters and circumstances the Board considers in determining dividend distribution, framed around a stated commitment to 'consistently reward its shareholders and deliver sustainable returns' commensurate with growth and performance. For FY2026, to mark the Bajaj Group's centenary year and Bajaj Auto's position as flagship company, the Board approved a one-off combined payout (dividend + share buyback via tender offer) equivalent to 100% of the year's profit after tax. Outside of that payout, the Board elected to retain the entire remaining profit for the year in distributable retained earnings (i.e., no separate transfer to general reserve). The Company maintains a policy of funding capex and strategic investments (e.g., in Bajaj Auto Credit, Bajaj Auto Technology, and the KTM restructuring) out of internal cash generation while preserving a healthy, surplus-cash balance sheet; it has not issued debt instruments or undertaken fixed deposit programmes and holds top-tier domestic credit ratings for its bank facilities.
currentContext.expansion: During FY2026 Bajaj Auto invested ~Rs 500 crore in capex and Rs 2,300+ crore in strategic bets (Bajaj Auto Credit Ltd. and Bajaj Auto International Holdings BV), funded from surplus cash generation, alongside meaningful investment across strategic priorities: growing its electric-mobility presence, scaling the Bajaj Auto Credit financing business, sharpening R&D capability through Bajaj Auto Technology Ltd., acquiring and assuming control over the KTM group, and widening its portfolio/footprint to capture domestic and international growth opportunities. The Directors' Report states the Company's current installed capacity at 7.2 million units per annum. Distribution/retail footprint expansion during the year included: 80 operational 'KT Showrooms' -- a new joint KTM-Triumph retail format; over 500 exclusive Chetak Experience Centres and more than 4,000 Chetak touchpoints; and, at the Brazil subsidiary (Bajaj Do Brasil), a manufacturing capacity ramp-up to 50,000 units per annum together with dealership network expansion to over 60 dealerships across 24 states. On the product/technology side, R&D was reorganised with expanded design, analysis and validation teams, several new test and prototyping facilities were added, and the IP portfolio grew via patent filings across Powertrain, Vehicle and Integration domains. Per BRSR Principle 2 disclosures, 55.9% of capex investment during FY2026 was directed to technologies with environmental/social benefit, specifically named as: 2-wheeler Chetak assembly and paint shop, 3-wheeler EV vehicle assembly, and dies and moulds. Bajaj Auto Technology Ltd. also developed alternate motor designs using light rare-earth magnets and established alternate geographic sourcing to restore Chetak supply after H1 disruption from Chinese rare-earth export restrictions.
currentContext.mdna: GST rationalisation in September 2025 (motorcycle rate up to 350cc cut from 28% to 18%) triggered a brief pre-cut pause followed by sharp H2 acceleration and record festive-season retail.|Domestic motorcycle industry grew 6.6% in FY2026 to ~13.1 million units (highest since FY2019), but the year was split into a flat/declining H1 and a strong double-digit H2.|125cc+ premiumisation is a structural driver, now 77.5% of total motorcycle sales, amid heightened competitive intensity in entry and mid-commuter categories.|Export recovery is a key driver: monthly export volumes crossed 2 lakh units in October 2025 for the first time in 39 months; LATAM delivered its best-ever year; East Africa and South Asia were the biggest growth drivers.|Margin improvement (EBITDA margin 20.5%, +30 bps YoY) driven by favourable USD/INR realisation, a profitable mix and operating leverage, which more than offset the margin-dilutive scale-up of electric two-wheeler sales and continued competitive investment.|Chetak volumes were constrained in H1 by non-availability of rare-earth magnets following Chinese export restrictions; supply was restored by end-September 2025 via alternate motor designs and alternate geographic sourcing, enabling a strong H2 recovery.|Resilient Indian macro backdrop -- GDP growth moderating to 6.5% (IMF) with private consumption near 56% of GDP, benign inflation enabling RBI rate cuts (repo rate to 5.25% by April 2026) -- supports domestic demand.|Management flags continuing margin pressure ahead from increasing commodity cost inflation, to be managed through disciplined operational execution.

risks.risk: Erosion of domestic motorcycle market share amid heightened competitive intensity
risks.note: Bajaj Auto's domestic motorcycle market share declined from 16.6% in FY2025 to 15.6% in FY2026 (BAL's own volumes grew only 0.6% versus 6.6% industry growth), driven by heightened competitive intensity particularly in the entry and mid-commuter categories.

Non-availability of rare earth magnets, a consequence of Chinese export restrictions, disrupted Chetak (EV) supply in H1 FY2026 and constrained volumes even as demand remained strong; management explicitly cites this as a supply-chain risk the company encountered during the year, remedied via alternate motor designs and alternate geographic sourcing.

risks.risk: Geopolitical and regulatory/macro-economic risk in export markets
risks.note: Management's Risk & Opportunities section explicitly flags geopolitical tensions and evolving regulatory and macroeconomic conditions in export markets as a dynamic risk requiring continuous scanning, relevant given the Company's substantial reliance on international/export revenue.

Management states it 'remains mindful of margin pressures arising from an increasing commodity pressure' going into the coming year, and that balancing growth and profitability against this will be a key operational task.

Currency volatility is explicitly named among the dynamic external risks scanned under the Company's Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework; FY2026 margins benefited from favourable USD/INR realisation, indicating margin sensitivity could reverse with currency moves.

Technological disruption is explicitly named as a risk category management continuously scans and anticipates under its ERM framework, relevant to the Company's ongoing ICE-to-EV transition across two- and three-wheelers.

Bajaj Auto acquired a controlling stake in KTM AG following the group's self-administration/restructuring proceedings in Austria; management states the turnaround is 'well underway' but not yet complete, with the aim to restore KTM to its original performance levels 'in due course' -- an unresolved execution risk on a newly-controlled, previously-distressed subsidiary.

one-line thesis: Record quarter on every line (vol 1.4m +29%, rev Rs.17,244 cr +37%, EBITDA Rs.3,596 cr +45%, PAT ~Rs.3,000 cr +42%) delivered *through* a hyperinflationary commodity shock (~4.5% of revenue), a ransomware shutdown and West-Asia supply disruptions that cost ~10% of volume. Margin still expanded to 20.9% (+110 bps YoY) on currency (USD-INR 94.4), mix and cost discipline. Exports (40% of rev) and EV (now 30% of domestic rev, double-digit EBITDA, Chetak turned EBITDA-positive) are the twin growth engines; capacity is now the binding constraint → 7m→9m units expansion underway.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):
| Metric | Q1 FY27 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Volumes | >1.4 m units | +29% | all-time high; ~10% volume lost to disruptions |
| Revenue (standalone) | Rs.17,244 cr | +37% | first time >Rs.17,000 cr |
| EBITDA | Rs.3,596 cr | +45% | all-time high |
| EBITDA margin | 20.9% | +110 bps YoY / +10 bps QoQ | despite ~4.5% commodity inflation |
| PAT (standalone) | ~Rs.3,000 cr | +42% | new high |
| Free cash flow | >Rs.2,300 cr | ~2x | ~80% cash conversion of PAT |
| Surplus cash | >Rs.21,000 cr | — | end-June (before July's ~Rs.10,000 cr payout) |
| Consol revenue | Rs.21,689 cr | +65% | NOT like-for-like (full qtr of KTM/Bajaj Mobility AG) |
| Consol PAT | Rs.3,226 cr | +46% | BACL + Brazil + KTM consolidation |
| Spares | Rs.1,700-1,800 cr | steady | record margins |

> **Consol +65% is not comparable** — first full quarter of line-by-line KTM (Bajaj Mobility AG) consolidation; base had none. Commodity inflation this single quarter exceeded the **prior two fiscal years combined**; pricing (Apr+Jun) offset ~half, currency + discretionary-cost cuts absorbed the rest.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Capacity: expand ~25% from 7 m to 9 m+ units/annum (medium term)** — priority to EV 2W & 3W, high-end motorcycles, 3W. Work already started.
- **Exports: cross 2,50,000 units/month "this quarter and onwards"** (from a base a few quarters ago of ~2,00,000).
- **EV 2W (Chetak) capacity: unlock 50,000 → 60,000 units immediate term** via productivity; demand > supply.
- **Portfolio makeover in next ~6 weeks (by Sept / by Oct meeting):** ~10 new variants/facelifts (160-400cc) + 2 brand-new Pulsars (a new 150cc and a new 125cc); plus **2 new brands in the 125cc segment within FY27** to upgrade 100cc customers.
- **Chetak network: 530-550 → ~1,000 exclusive stores in "a couple of years."**
- **Electric portfolio EBITDA: stays double-digit** (Chetak now EBITDA-positive).
- **Cash: rebuild to ~Rs.15,000 cr by FY27-end** (target level) after July's ~Rs.10,000 cr shareholder payout.
- Q2 to reflect broader inflation (proprietary components, electronics, labour, logistics, energy) over the full period — no precise number given ("premature").
order book & pipeline: Not order-book; demand-led. Domestic demand "very positive," export demand strong in key markets. Product pipeline is the near-term catalyst (10+ launches in 6 weeks; 2 new 125cc brands in FY27; new Triumph products on the anvil). Supply-chain disruption expected to ease in Q2, aiding top line.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Exports (40% of rev):** 7,32,000 units, USD 735 m; grew >2x industry in top-30 markets. Africa: industry +50%, Bajaj doubled retail (~60% retail share), Nigeria led (pre-election). LatAm: Mexico now top-5 world market (3% tariff advantage), Brazil retail +50% (75+ stores). Asia muted (Bangladesh/Nepal weak). KTM India exports +20%, Triumph exports +40% YoY. **3W exports record 100,000 units, +~70%, >65% share.**
- **Domestic 2W:** industry registrations +14% (vs +25% Q4); motorcycle industry +7%. 150cc+ growing 1.5x industry; N/NS series ~60% of 150cc+ sales; +couple pts Vahan share in 5 months.
- **Pro-Biking (KTM+Triumph):** combined domestic ~40,000 units, +50% YoY; ~90 joint KTM-Triumph stores; Triumph in ~210-215 touchpoints.
- **Chetak (EV scooter):** +65-80% YoY, highest-ever qtr volume/rev/profitability; EV now ~25% of ICE scooters (>50% in some states); 530+ stores / 4,500 touchpoints / 850+ cities.
- **Commercial vehicles (3W):** industry +11% (e-autos now 44% of L5); ICE share ~70%; EV leadership; Riki (L3 e-rick) in ~150 cities; 12-model electric 3W range.
- **BACL (financing):** total income >Rs.1,100 cr; PAT Rs.227 cr (>2x YoY); **AUM Rs.20,000 cr (+70% YoY)**; CAR 19%; ROE >25%.
- **KTM AG:** first full quarter of consolidation; turnaround "in line with roadmap" — production ramped, inventories normalized, fixed-cost control showing.
growth verticals / optionality:
- EV 2W+3W = 30% of domestic revenue at double-digit EBITDA — a scaled, profitable second engine (Bajaj entered scooters only in 2020 via electric Chetak, already #2 at ~23-24% share).
- KTM India-manufacturing: "substantial" manufacturing to shift to India (China+1/+2), co-development between Bajaj & KTM R&D resumed with "more strength" — but KTM run independently, on arm's-length competitive terms (not declared a "global hub").
- 3W e-rick (Riki) as a funnel to upgrade lead-acid drivers to lithium e-autos.
6a. moat & competitive position (optiona:
- **Export franchise depth:** >60% retail share in Nigeria on the Boxer brand + wide service network; Mexico competitiveness from local supply chain + 3% best-tariff position — durable distribution/brand advantages, not just price.
- **Brand-led premium play:** deliberate 4-brand architecture (Pulsar/Dominar/KTM/Triumph) to challenge entrenched players "with the right brand," explicitly refusing to "buy market share" — pricing power protected.
- **3W ICE leadership ~70% share** + widest (12-model) electric 3W portfolio — scale + range breadth as a barrier.
margins & cost dynamics: Margin bridge: hyperinflation (steel +10%, aluminium/platinum/rhodium ~+40%) hit GM; ~half recovered via calibrated Apr+Jun pricing; remainder absorbed by (a) favourable USD-INR (realized 94.4 vs 90.6 QoQ, 85.6 YoY), (b) richer mix (CVs, premium, exports, EV), (c) operating leverage on record volume, (d) discretionary + fixed-cost discipline (other-expenses down % of sales). EV profitability improving on scale + value engineering. Q2 risk: inflation broadening beyond metals into components/electronics/labour/energy.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Capacity expansion 7m→9m+ units/annum (~25%+), fungible across BUs (hence no BU-level number yet). Chetak 50k→60k immediate; further EV 2W/3W, high-end bikes, wide-body 3W to follow. Chetak store network to ~1,000 in a couple of years.
capital allocation: **100% payout of FY26 profit (Rs.9,825 cr)** via hybrid base-dividend + buyback (buyback concluded last week; ~Rs.10,000 cr total to shareholders in July — buyback route chosen for post-Finance-Act tax attractiveness to non-promoters). Cash to dip from >Rs.21,000 cr then rebuild to ~Rs.15,000 cr target by FY27-end on ~80% cash conversion.
risks & watch-items:
- **Commodity super-cycle broadening** into components/electronics/labour/logistics/energy — Q2 to feel fuller impact; pricing is "one lever, not the only one."
- **Currency dependence:** margin cushion hinges on a weak rupee; RBI measures could reverse it.
- **Operational fragility exposed:** ransomware shutdown + LPG/fuel curtailment + West-Asia force-majeure + election-driven labour shortage cost ~10% volume this quarter — recurrence risk.
- **Bottom-of-pyramid weakness:** 100cc/125cc growing low-single-digit; Bajaj ceding 100cc share by choice (profitability over volume) → wholesale market share drifting down.
- KTM comparability/normalization over coming quarters; consol optics inflated by consolidation.
management quality / tone: Highly confident, granular, strategically candid. Rakesh Sharma frank on trade-offs ("participate in 100cc on our own terms… prepared to lose market share"; "we will not buy market share"). Dinesh Thapar disciplined and specific on the inflation bridge and capital return. Playful but precise ("you guys are not taking me seriously… 10 models in 6 weeks"). Proactively returned to an unanswered EV-profitability question at close.
non-obvious takeaways:
- Reported records **understate** underlying: ~10% volume was lost to one-off shocks — true run-rate was tracking >1.5m units.
- EV surge (+67-70%) is being driven by petrol-price fear post West-Asia crisis and is **cannibalizing ICE scooters specifically** (range parity with scooters, not motorcycles) — a demand-mix, not just subsidy, story.
- Consol growth flatters via KTM full-quarter consolidation — watch standalone + BACL for clean signal; BACL AUM Rs.20,000 cr (+70%), ROE >25% is a quietly large financing engine.
- 100% FY26 payout + buyback signals capital-return discipline while still funding a 25% capacity build — cash machine funding both.

LatAm: Mexico now top-5 world market (3% tariff advantage), Brazil retail +50% (75+ stores). Asia muted (Bangladesh/Nepal weak). KTM India exports +20%, Triumph exports +40% YoY. **3W exports record 100,000 units, +~70%, >65% share.**
- **Domestic 2W:** industry registrations +14% (vs +25% Q4); motorcycle industry +7%. 150cc+ growing 1.5x industry; N/NS series ~60% of 150cc+ sales; +couple pts Vahan share in 5 months.
- **Pro-Biking (KTM+Triumph):** combined domestic ~40,000 units, +50% YoY; ~90 joint KTM-Triumph stores; Triumph in ~210-215 touchpoints.
- **Chetak (EV scooter):** +65-80% YoY, highest-ever qtr volume/rev/profitability; EV now ~25% of ICE scooters (>50% in some states); 530+ stores / 4,500 touchpoints / 850+ cities.
- **Commercial vehicles (3W):** industry +11% (e-autos now 44% of L5); ICE share ~70%; EV leadership; Riki (L3 e-rick) in ~150 cities; 12-model electric 3W range.
- **BACL (financing):** total income >Rs.1,100 cr; PAT Rs.227 cr (>2x YoY); **AUM Rs.20,000 cr (+70% YoY)**; CAR 19%; ROE >25%.
- **KTM AG:** first full quarter of consolidation; turnaround "in line with roadmap" — production ramped, inventories normalized, fixed-cost control showing.
growth verticals / optionality:
- EV 2W+3W = 30% of domestic revenue at double-digit EBITDA — a scaled, profitable second engine (Bajaj entered scooters only in 2020 via electric Chetak, already #2 at ~23-24% share).
- KTM India-manufacturing: "substantial" manufacturing to shift to India (China+1/+2), co-development between Bajaj & KTM R&D resumed with "more strength" — but KTM run independently, on arm's-length competitive terms (not declared a "global hub").
- 3W e-rick (Riki) as a funnel to upgrade lead-acid drivers to lithium e-autos.
6a. moat & competitive position (optiona:
- **Export franchise depth:** >60% retail share in Nigeria on the Boxer brand + wide service network; Mexico competitiveness from local supply chain + 3% best-tariff position — durable distribution/brand advantages, not just price.
- **Brand-led premium play:** deliberate 4-brand architecture (Pulsar/Dominar/KTM/Triumph) to challenge entrenched players "with the right brand," explicitly refusing to "buy market share" — pricing power protected.
- **3W ICE leadership ~70% share** + widest (12-model) electric 3W portfolio — scale + range breadth as a barrier.
margins & cost dynamics: Margin bridge: hyperinflation (steel +10%, aluminium/platinum/rhodium ~+40%) hit GM; ~half recovered via calibrated Apr+Jun pricing; remainder absorbed by (a) favourable USD-INR (realized 94.4 vs 90.6 QoQ, 85.6 YoY), (b) richer mix (CVs, premium, exports, EV), (c) operating leverage on record volume, (d) discretionary + fixed-cost discipline (other-expenses down % of sales). EV profitability improving on scale + value engineering. Q2 risk: inflation broadening beyond metals into components/electronics/labour/energy.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Capacity expansion 7m→9m+ units/annum (~25%+), fungible across BUs (hence no BU-level number yet). Chetak 50k→60k immediate; further EV 2W/3W, high-end bikes, wide-body 3W to follow. Chetak store network to ~1,000 in a couple of years.
capital allocation: **100% payout of FY26 profit (Rs.9,825 cr)** via hybrid base-dividend + buyback (buyback concluded last week; ~Rs.10,000 cr total to shareholders in July — buyback route chosen for post-Finance-Act tax attractiveness to non-promoters). Cash to dip from >Rs.21,000 cr then rebuild to ~Rs.15,000 cr target by FY27-end on ~80% cash conversion.
risks & watch-items:
- **Commodity super-cycle broadening** into components/electronics/labour/logistics/energy — Q2 to feel fuller impact; pricing is "one lever, not the only one."
- **Currency dependence:** margin cushion hinges on a weak rupee; RBI measures could reverse it.
- **Operational fragility exposed:** ransomware shutdown + LPG/fuel curtailment + West-Asia force-majeure + election-driven labour shortage cost ~10% volume this quarter — recurrence risk.
- **Bottom-of-pyramid weakness:** 100cc/125cc growing low-single-digit; Bajaj ceding 100cc share by choice (profitability over volume) → wholesale market share drifting down.
- KTM comparability/normalization over coming quarters; consol optics inflated by consolidation.
management quality / tone: Highly confident, granular, strategically candid. Rakesh Sharma frank on trade-offs ("participate in 100cc on our own terms… prepared to lose market share"; "we will not buy market share"). Dinesh Thapar disciplined and specific on the inflation bridge and capital return. Playful but precise ("you guys are not taking me seriously… 10 models in 6 weeks"). Proactively returned to an unanswered EV-profitability question at close.
non-obvious takeaways:
- Reported records **understate** underlying: ~10% volume was lost to one-off shocks — true run-rate was tracking >1.5m units.
- EV surge (+67-70%) is being driven by petrol-price fear post West-Asia crisis and is **cannibalizing ICE scooters specifically** (range parity with scooters, not motorcycles) — a demand-mix, not just subsidy, story.
- Consol growth flatters via KTM full-quarter consolidation — watch standalone + BACL for clean signal; BACL AUM Rs.20,000 cr (+70%), ROE >25% is a quietly large financing engine.

themes.title: Auto OEM cycle - CV replacement & PV premiumization
themes.need: GST 2.0 rate rationalization plus an aged CV fleet still frames the replacement cycle, but Q1FY27's real signal is 2W OEMs EXPANDING margin through a commodity shock. TVSMOTOR sold 1.63mn units (+28%) on INR 13,896cr revenue (+38%) while lifting EBITDA margin 30bps to 12.8% having absorbed a ~4% commodity shock with only ~1.5% of price increase (CARE upgraded it AA+ to AAA), and committed 2W capacity from 6.8mn to 8.3mn by Q4FY27. BAJAJ-AUTO set volume/revenue/EBITDA records with margin at 20.9% (+110bps) through ~4.5% commodity inflation AND ~10% of volume lost to a ransomware shutdown, with EV now 30% of domestic revenue at double-digit EBITDA and Chetak EBITDA-positive - a scaled, profitable EV second engine. Commercial mobility is electrifying fastest: TVSMOTOR's 3W EV penetration crossed 40% for the first time. ASHOKLEY's all-time-high CV volumes (220k units, MHCV share 30.8%) carry the CV leg with defence + Switch EV optionality; TMCV/TMPV/SMLMAH/ESCORTS on CV/tractors; APOLLOTYRE/JKTYRE/BALKRISIND/MRF on tyres.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Bajaj Auto manufactures and sells motorcycles (commuter to premium sports bikes), electric scooters, and ICE/CNG/electric three-wheelers (passenger and goods carriers) plus the Qute quadricycle, along with related parts and accessories. It serves customers pan-India and in over 100 countries, spanning domestic retail, commercial/fleet buyers and export markets, with premium global motorcycle portfolios under KTM and Triumph.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- GST rationalisation in September 2025 (motorcycle rate up to 350cc cut from 28% to 18%) triggered a brief pre-cut pause followed by sharp H2 acceleration and record festive-season retail.
- Domestic motorcycle industry grew 6.6% in FY2026 to ~13.1 million units (highest since FY2019), but the year was split into a flat/declining H1 and a strong double-digit H2.
- 125cc+ premiumisation is a structural driver, now 77.5% of total motorcycle sales, amid heightened competitive intensity in entry and mid-commuter categories.
- Export recovery is a key driver: monthly export volumes crossed 2 lakh units in October 2025 for the first time in 39 months; LATAM delivered its best-ever year; East Africa and South Asia were the biggest growth drivers.
- Margin improvement (EBITDA margin 20.5%, +30 bps YoY) driven by favourable USD/INR realisation, a profitable mix and operating leverage, which more than offset the margin-dilutive scale-up of electric two-wheeler sales and continued competitive investment.
- Chetak volumes were constrained in H1 by non-availability of rare-earth magnets following Chinese export restrictions; supply was restored by end-September 2025 via alternate motor designs and alternate geographic sourcing, enabling a strong H2 recovery.
- Resilient Indian macro backdrop -- GDP growth moderating to 6.5% (IMF) with private consumption near 56% of GDP, benign inflation enabling RBI rate cuts (repo rate to 5.25% by April 2026) -- supports domestic demand.
- Management flags continuing margin pressure ahead from increasing commodity cost inflation, to be managed through disciplined operational execution.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: During FY2026 Bajaj Auto invested ~Rs 500 crore in capex and Rs 2,300+ crore in strategic bets (Bajaj Auto Credit Ltd. and Bajaj Auto International Holdings BV), funded from surplus cash generation, alongside meaningful investment across strategic priorities: growing its electric-mobility presence, scaling the Bajaj Auto Credit financing business, sharpening R&D capability through Bajaj Auto Technology Ltd., acquiring and assuming control over the KTM group, and widening its portfolio/footprint to capture domestic and international growth opportunities. The Directors' Report states the Company's current installed capacity at 7.2 million units per annum. Distribution/retail footprint expansion during the year included: 80 operational 'KT Showrooms' -- a new joint KTM-Triumph retail format; over 500 exclusive Chetak Experience Centres and more than 4,000 Chetak touchpoints; and, at the Brazil subsidiary (Bajaj Do Brasil), a manufacturing capacity ramp-up to 50,000 units per annum together with dealership network expansion to over 60 dealerships across 24 states. On the product/technology side, R&D was reorganised with expanded design, analysis and validation teams, several new test and prototyping facilities were added, and the IP portfolio grew via patent filings across Powertrain, Vehicle and Integration domains. Per BRSR Principle 2 disclosures, 55.9% of capex investment during FY2026 was directed to technologies with environmental/social benefit, specifically named as: 2-wheeler Chetak assembly and paint shop, 3-wheeler EV vehicle assembly, and dies and moulds. Bajaj Auto Technology Ltd. also developed alternate motor designs using light rare-earth magnets and established alternate geographic sourcing to restore Chetak supply after H1 disruption from Chinese rare-earth export restrictions.
